verdict.rationale: Supabase documents multiple mechanisms for scoping agent credentials: publishable vs. secret keys tied to RLS, MCP server flags (read_only=true, project_ref scoping, feature-group toggles disabling account/write tools), and a live OAuth-protected MCP endpoint exposing granular per-scope permissions (projects:read, database:write, storage:read, etc., per supabase-probe-10). However the docs themselves admit PATs used for CI 'require all scopes' for write access rather than fine-grained ones (supabase-supp-mcp-agent-security), and community evidence shows a real-world case where an AI assistant operated via service_role, bypassing RLS entirely (supabase-comm-15) — a concrete gap against the least-privilege ideal. Missing for 10: fully granular PAT/API-key scoping (not just MCP OAuth scopes), and stronger community corroboration that least-privilege defaults are actually followed in practice rather than requiring manual read_only/project_ref configuration.
